input.question: Why does a hearing a recording of my voice sound different to me then when I hear myself talk?
input.ground_truth: We hear sounds as vibrations hitting our ear drums. When we hear most sounds, these vibrations travel through the air and into the ear canal. Our own voices also vibrate through our bodies, creating a slightly lower pitch. When you hear a recording of your voice you are missing this extra level of vibration that lowers the sound, so your voice sounds higher than what you are used to. Source: _URL_0_

Question: Why does a hearing a recording of my voice sound different to me then when I hear myself talk?

Answer:

response.prediction: When you hear your voice while speaking, you are actually hearing a combination of the sound waves coming from your vocal cords and the vibrations that travel through your skull, jaw, and bones in your head. These bone vibrations add depth and richness to your voice that you don’t notice because you are used to it. However, when you listen to a recording, you only hear the sound waves traveling through the air, which lack those internal vibrations. As a result, your recorded voice may sound higher, lower, or just different from what you expect, because it is missing the extra resonance you hear when you speak normally.
